question: An engineer is analyzing traces from a service that intermittently throttles under load. The traces capture several response headers and fields per call. Select all of the following that are directly useful for diagnosing why a specific call was throttled and when it will be safe to retry.
options: A) retry-after, showing the number of seconds to wait before a retry is likely to succeed
B) anthropic-ratelimit-input-tokens-reset, showing when the input-token portion of the limit will be replenished
C) content-type, showing the MIME type Anthropic used to encode the JSON response body
D) anthropic-ratelimit-tokens-remaining, showing the tokens remaining under the currently most restrictive limit in effect
E) anthropic-ratelimit-requests-remaining, showing how many requests remain before the caller is rate limited
correct_answers: A) retry-after, showing the number of seconds to wait before a retry is likely to succeed
B) anthropic-ratelimit-input-tokens-reset, showing when the input-token portion of the limit will be replenished
D) anthropic-ratelimit-tokens-remaining, showing the tokens remaining under the currently most restrictive limit in effect
E) anthropic-ratelimit-requests-remaining, showing how many requests remain before the caller is rate limited
explanations: Correct: retry-after is the documented signal for exactly how long to wait before a retry is expected to succeed.
Correct: this header pinpoints when the input-token limit specifically will replenish, which is useful when input-token consumption (rather than request count) is the binding constraint.
Incorrect: content-type only describes the response body's encoding format and carries no information about rate-limit state or throttling.
Correct: this header reflects whichever limit (organization or workspace) is currently most restrictive, giving direct insight into the binding constraint behind a throttling event.
Correct: this header directly shows the caller's remaining request quota, which is useful for anticipating and diagnosing throttling before or after it occurs.
